pointers.sentence: Without `LoginRequiredMiddleware` (5.1) a view is open unless a decorator or a mixin closes it; with it, after `AuthenticationMiddleware`, every view is closed to an anonymous request unless the decorator `login_not_required` (5.1) opens it (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:LoginRequiredMiddleware.process_view`).

5.0 added the functions `aauthenticate`, `aget_user`, `alogin`, `alogout` and `aupdate_session_auth_hash` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py`) with `HttpRequest.auser`, 5.1 the session store's coroutines, such as `SessionBase.aget` ([The session store: `SessionBase`](../auth/sessions.md#the-asynchronous-methods)), and 5.2 `UserManager.acreate_user`, `PermissionsMixin.ahas_perm` and the other permission methods' coroutines, and those of the backends.
`aauthenticate` picks the backends by the signature of their synchronous `authenticate`, then awaits each one's `BaseBackend.aauthenticate` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:aauthenticate`).

`BaseBackend.aauthenticate` wraps `authenticate` in `sync_to_async`, but since 5.2 `ModelBackend` and `RemoteUserBackend` have their own, on the asynchronous ORM, to "reduce context-switching", the 5.2 notes say (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend.aauthenticate`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

`BaseBackend.aauthenticate` wraps `authenticate` in `sync_to_async`, but since 5.2 `ModelBackend` and `RemoteUserBackend` have their own, on the asynchronous ORM, to "reduce context-switching", the 5.2 notes say (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend.aauthenticate`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

`PermissionsMixin.ahas_perm` asks only the backends that have an `ahas_perm` (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:_auser_has_perm`; [Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](../auth/authenticating.md#aauthenticate-and-basebackend)).
The documentation asks a project extending Django's backends to change both (`docs/topics/auth/customizing.txt`).

`RemoteUserMiddleware`, which logs in the user a server names, is not built on `MiddlewareMixin`; it can run either way, and so takes the mode of the layer inside it, the next in `MIDDLEWARE` (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

In an asynchronous chain `RemoteUserMiddleware.__call__` hands the request to `RemoteUserMiddleware.aprocess_request` alone, in a synchronous one to `RemoteUserMiddleware.process_request` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware.__call__`).
5.2.0 and 5.2.1 had lost it (`docs/releases/5.2.2.txt`).

Since 6.1 `RemoteUserMiddleware.get_username` serves both paths, adding the prefix only to the default header of an `ASGIRequest` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware.get_username`); a custom header the synchronous path always read as written ([Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](../auth/authenticating.md#the-servers-user-remoteusermiddleware-and-remoteuserbackend)).

From 5.2 `login` and `alogin` warned when given `None`, and logged in the request's user; 6.1 removed the fallback, and both ask the user they are given for its session hash first (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`).
Since 6.1 `login` and `logout` replace `HttpRequest.auser` as they replace `user` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_set_auth_user`).

`PBKDF2PasswordHasher`, first in the default `PASSWORD_HASHERS`, has had more iterations in every feature release, 720,000 in 5.0 and 870,000 in 5.1 (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:PBKDF2PasswordHasher`).

A stored string carries its own count and still checks, but `PBKDF2PasswordHasher.must_update` compares the count with the class's, and a right password checked against an older string is hashed again and saved (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.check_password`; [Password hashing: `make_password` and the hashers](../auth/hashers.md#the-upgrade-at-a-login)).
CryptPasswordHasher went in 5.0, and SHA1PasswordHasher, UnsaltedSHA1PasswordHasher and UnsaltedMD5PasswordHasher in 5.1 (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`).
CryptPasswordHasher went in 5.0, and SHA1PasswordHasher, UnsaltedSHA1PasswordHasher and UnsaltedMD5PasswordHasher in 5.1 (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`).

A project still naming one in `PASSWORD_HASHERS` can neither check nor make a password, since `get_hashers` imports every class of the list: under 5.2.17 as at this commit, a check raises `ImportError` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:get_hashers`).
With the name gone, the string finds no hasher, and `verify_password` answers it as a wrong password, without a warning (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:verify_password`).

Since 6.1 `SessionBase.__bool__` answers the opposite of `SessionBase.is_empty`: false for a store with no key and no data, without loading (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.__bool__`; [The session store: `SessionBase`](../auth/sessions.md#empty-is_empty-and-__bool)).
